title: Durable processing and recovery

subtasks.description: Align queue names and worker subscriptions explicitly; add a real broker-to-worker smoke test.
subtasks.progress_note: Queue contract: PROCESSING_QUEUE is the routed queue, the declared task_queues entry and the worker default (backend/celery_app); Makefile and infra/compose worker commands pass --queues processing; stale routes removed. Regression tests incl. an in-process broker-to-worker smoke test (memory transport, Redis variant when TEST_REDIS_URL is set) that times out with the old configuration. Verified locally (104 passed on PostgreSQL). Redis-backed variant not yet observed locally or in remote CI. Product commit 1a25b861.

subtasks.description: Commit job and outbox event atomically, then publish with retry and acknowledgement tracking.
subtasks.progress_note: job_dispatches outbox row committed with the job (create_upload_job); dispatch_job publishes under FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and records the broker message id; exponential backoff to DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS then FAILED (visible via JobResponse.dispatch); sweep_dispatch_outbox as Celery beat task + `python -m backend.jobs.outbox`; cancel on meeting deletion; payload workspace assertion re-checked against the persisted job; at-least-once documented (ADR 0007). RLS: 'dispatch' service scope on job_dispatches only. Migration e5a7c3d9b1f2 backfills queued jobs. Verified locally: test_dispatch_outbox.py (rollback, outage/backoff/park, lost-mark redelivery without duplicate results/usage, cancellation + late delivery, mismatched payload, competing dispatchers on PostgreSQL, scope visibility) and the memory-transport worker smoke test through the outbox; 148 passed on PostgreSQL 16.15, 138+10 skipped on SQLite. Evidence label: the broker test is a Celery worker integration test on the in-memory transport (real worker thread, same process); it does not validate Redis, network transport, cross-process delivery or deployed broker durability. Not verified: Redis-backed variant (TEST_REDIS_URL unset locally; runs in CI), beat in a deployed stack. Product commit 7bc47c88. Since T04 the same outbox row is re-armed for retries and recovery (dispatch.generation).

subtasks.description: Add stage attempts/checkpoints with immutable input hashes and idempotent artifact/result writes.
subtasks.progress_note: Validated in local scope (product commit 5c7ada2a). backend/jobs/checkpoints.py: a completed ASR/diarization/analysis result is committed as a stage checkpoint — PENDING row declared under the lease fence with an attempt-scoped object key (art-<attempt id>-<stage>), object written through the storage abstraction and read back (size, SHA-256, strict schema), fenced publication (PUBLISHED) recording provider usage; input_hash = SHA-256 of a canonical manifest of declared inputs (scope, stage contract/schema version, recording digest and size, materialise version, ProviderIdentity with model and result-affecting params, request params, upstream artifact digests + turns version) — never attempt/worker ids or times. Reuse only for PUBLISHED rows with matching identity/schema, live meeting and recording, and an artifact that verifies; missing/corrupt artifacts are invalidated under the fence and recomputed; a newer verified result supersedes an older row of the same identity (partial unique index keeps one PUBLISHED row per meeting/stage/hash). Storage: put_stream(object_token) idempotent on content, object_conflict on different content, object_incomplete; S3 conditional create. Deletion retires checkpoints and objects; cleanup sweep (beat stage-artifact-cleanup / python -m backend.jobs.checkpoints) removes objects of non-published or invalidated rows after JOB_ARTIFACT_GRACE_SECONDS, never a published artifact of a live meeting, never a PENDING row whose job is RUNNING at that generation. Migration c8d1e5f7a2b4 (table under tenant RLS, checkpoint_id/reused on processing_stage_runs). test_stage_checkpoints.py (18): identity determinism/exclusions; reuse with one recomputation; targeted invalidation on ASR model change (diarization reused) and on analysis contract change; crash after checkpoints resumes with zero provider calls and one settlement; missing/corrupt artifacts never a hit; load bound/schema/cross-tenant key rejection; reuse disabled supersedes; incomplete write not successful (ABANDONED, no object); crash before publication leaves PENDING + object, cleaned after grace, winner untouched; cleanup respects live lease; idempotent writes/conflicts; stale worker cannot declare/publish (only winner's 3 objects exist); conflicting attempt refused by fence and by the index; deletion racing publication leaves nothing; deleting a processed meeting retires objects; RLS hides/refuses other tenant; API stage provenance. Full suite 208 passed on PostgreSQL 16.15 (homayar_app, one worker), 186 passed + 22 skipped on SQLite; check-migrations.sh exit 0, downgrade/upgrade round trip, 28 forced policies. Unverified: real S3 conditional writes, Redis-backed transport, deployed beat.

subtasks.description: Implement lease renewal, fencing tokens and a sweeper for abandoned work; reject stale worker commits.
subtasks.progress_note: Execution lease on processing_jobs (locked_by/locked_at, lease_generation fencing token, attempt_id, lease_expires_at, lease_renewed_at; RUNNING rows must carry owner + lease). Atomic claim against PostgreSQL now(); renewal (LeaseHeartbeat every JOB_LEASE_RENEW_INTERVAL_SECONDS, never past the attempt deadline) and every protected write (stage transition, results, completion, failure, usage settlement, post-success audio deletion) re-lock the row and require state/generation/owner/unexpired lease; a stale attempt reports superseded and writes nothing. Stage timeout via wait_for; Celery soft/hard time limits as last bound. Retryable failures requeue through the outbox (rearm_dispatch with generation), no broker task.retry. Recovery sweeper (backend.jobs.recovery; beat entry job-lease-recovery, CLI) discovers expired RUNNING attempts under the read-only 'recovery' RLS scope, fences the generation, records the abandoned stage, re-arms the intent or parks dead_letter (failure_code lease_expired, reservations released) when attempts are exhausted. Migration f1b6d8e4a2c7 (backfills running rows as expired; drain workers before upgrade). Verified locally: test_job_leases.py on PostgreSQL 16.15 — competing claims (one lease), renewal accepted/rejected (other owner, guessed generation, expired, deadline), heartbeat under a blocked stage, recovery + fence + re-arm + audit/stage rows, stale worker rejected for results/terminal status/failure/usage/audio deletion, resumed stale worker after recovery cannot overwrite the new attempt, old messages inert, deletion racing renewal/recovery, exhaustion -> dead_letter, stage timeout -> retry via outbox, recovery scope reads processing_jobs only and cannot write, no context leak on connection reuse; full suite 162 passed on PostgreSQL, 148 passed + 14 skipped on SQLite; migration upgrade/check/downgrade/upgrade on PostgreSQL and SQLite. Not verified: Redis transport, deployed beat, hard time limit in a real Celery pool, PgBouncer. Product commit 59c8ff45.

subtasks.description: Define cancellation, retryability, deadlines, poison/dead-letter behavior and bounded retry budgets.
subtasks.progress_note: Failure classes persisted on processing_jobs.failure_class (publication / transient / permanent / abandoned / deadline / cancelled) next to failure_code; failed is final (permanent), dead_letter parks everything replayable (exhausted publication, exhausted transient/abandoned attempts, deadline), cancelled is final; parking always drops the lease, releases both reservations and reflects the meeting (backend/jobs/failures.py, ADR 0009). Retry budget: JOB_MAX_ATTEMPTS per replay window, exponential back-off JOB_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS doubling to JOB_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_SECONDS through the job's own outbox row, one deadline_at per job (JOB_DEADLINE_SECONDS) enforced at claim, when a retry is scheduled and in recovery. Exhausted publication dead-letters the job in the publisher's transaction (job context then the persisted tenant; dispatch scope alone cannot touch jobs). Meeting deletion cancels through one helper. Operator replay POST /api/v1/admin/jobs/{id}/replay (workspace:manage + CSRF, route recorded in the authorization matrix): bounded by JOB_MAX_REPLAYS, fresh max_attempts on top of recorded attempts (history kept), new deadline, quota re-reserved under the current entitlement (429 when it does not fit, nothing written), refuses deleted meetings / missing recordings / expired retention / non-dead-letter states, advances the lease generation, re-arms and publishes the intent, audited as meeting.processing.replayed. Migration a7d2c4e9f6b1 (classifies legacy terminal rows). Verified locally: test_job_failure_policy.py (11) — back-off + exhaustion, permanent failure, deadline at retry/claim/recovery, publication exhaustion parks atomically and replay runs the job with one settlement on the new reservation, replay bounded and refused for queued/running/completed, quota/recording/retention/deleted-meeting refusals leave the job untouched, cross-workspace job invisible, member denied / CSRF required / actor audited, deletion cancels with the class, attempts from before a replay cannot write after it, settings validation; full suite 173 passed on PostgreSQL 16.15 (homayar_app via SET ROLE, one worker), 159 passed + 14 skipped on SQLite; check-migrations.sh on a disposable PostgreSQL database exit 0 (27 policies, none enabled-but-not-forced), downgrade/upgrade round-trip on PostgreSQL and SQLite; ruff clean on changed files. Not verified: Redis transport, deployed beat, a real Celery pool. Not in scope: a customer-facing cancel endpoint (deletion is the cancellation path), stage checkpoints (T03), stable usage-event identity (T06), fault injection (T07). Product commit 9dde0a0d.

subtasks.description: Make usage and downstream events idempotent even when processing is delivered more than once.
subtasks.progress_note: usage_events is now an append-only ledger of every reservation transition (reserved / committed / released, plus reconciliation adjusted) keyed by a unique operation_key (<reservation id>:<type>, or a reconciliation identity) with (reservation, type) unique and a reason column; reserve_usage/commit_usage/release_usage stay idempotent under the reservation row lock and the unique keys are the database backstop (ADR 0010). Settlement invariant in PostgreSQL: partial unique index uq_reservation_settled_per_meeting allows one COMMITTED reservation per meeting and metric, so retries, redeliveries, recovery and replay cannot charge twice; identities are stable (upload key for the first reservation, replay:<job>:<n> per replay, the job's reservation across attempts — no new identity per retry). Reconciliation (backend/jobs/usage_reconciliation.py; beat usage-reconciliation every USAGE_RECONCILIATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS, CLI with --repair) discovers entitlements under the read-only usage_reconciliation RLS scope, reconciles each in a tenant-bound transaction holding the entitlement FOR UPDATE: RESERVED rows older than the grace period with a deleted meeting or no queued/running job are released (reconciled_orphan); counters are compared with the reservation rows; drift is logged and audited (usage.reconciled, outcome failure) and corrected only when USAGE_RECONCILIATION_REPAIR_COUNTERS/--repair is set, through one idempotent adjusted row. Migration b9e4f2a6c8d3 (backfills operation keys, refuses to run on duplicate settlements, downgrade deletes non-committed ledger rows and restores the legacy unique). UsageEventResponse exposes operation_key/reason. Verified locally: test_usage_ledger.py (9) — each transition recorded once with stable keys and visible via the billing API, database refuses a second committed row and a second COMMITTED reservation per meeting/metric, dead-letter -> replay -> completion -> duplicate delivery charges once, concurrent settlement commits once (PostgreSQL), reconciliation releases orphans / ignores live reservations / reports drift without touching counters / repairs once on request / inert afterwards, reconciliation scope reads entitlements only and cannot write (PostgreSQL), settings validation; existing lease/entitlement/billing tests updated to count settlements rather than every ledger row (intended contract change). Full suite 181 passed on PostgreSQL 16.15 (homayar_app via SET ROLE, one worker), 165 passed + 16 skipped on SQLite; check-migrations.sh on a disposable PostgreSQL database exit 0 (27 policies, none enabled-but-not-forced; entitlements policy carries the usage_reconciliation scope; partial index and unique constraints present), downgrade/upgrade round-trip on PostgreSQL and SQLite; ruff clean on changed files. Not verified: Redis transport, deployed beat. Not in scope: billing periods / counter rollover and invoice reconciliation (WP18), webhook delivery idempotency (WP16), the empty-transcript charging policy (ADR 0003, open), fault injection (T07). Product commit 2e702777.

subtasks.description: Inject worker kill, broker restart, lost acknowledgement, duplicate delivery and object-write failure; reconcile all accepted jobs.
subtasks.progress_note: In-process fault model validated: backend/jobs/invariants.py is a read-only checker of the durable-processing promises per workspace (running lease, terminal released, queued delivery path, reservations match state, single settlement, ledger vs counters, meeting status) with an operator CLI over all workspaces (discovery under the usage_reconciliation scope, tenant-bound inspection, exit 1 on violations; recorded in the runbook's Maintenance Checks). test_fault_injection.py (5): transient storage-read faults plus a broker outage with every message delivered twice converge to completed with one settlement per meeting (attempt 2 after the transient failure, retries through the outbox row); a worker killed mid-stage (gated provider, lease expired) is recovered by the sweep, a healthy worker completes, the resumed writer is superseded; lost acknowledgement redelivered during and after an attempt is inert; an object delete failure after success keeps results and the single charge without pretending deletion; injected corruption (settled reservation reverted, queued job with a withdrawn intent) is reported by rule and counted by the CLI summary. All scenarios end with an empty violation list. Full suite 186 passed on PostgreSQL 16.15 (one worker), fault module 3 passed + 2 skipped (threaded scenarios are PostgreSQL-only) on SQLite; ruff clean. Not run / blocked_external: a real Celery pool kill (hard time limit), a real broker restart on Redis/network transport, transport-level lost acknowledgement (only the memory-transport worker test of T01 exists), object-write failures for worker outputs (no worker object writes until T03), deployed beat. Status partial until a Redis-backed or deployed-stack drill is observed. Product commit 787bed6e. Session 7 (2026-09-10, product 5c7ada2a): artifact-write faults inside the worker now exist and are injected (test_fault_injection.py: two artifact writes fail transiently with a broker outage and duplicate delivery; jobs converge, ABANDONED write_failed rows have no object, one settlement per meeting, invariants clean with storage); the checker gained checkpoint_state and artifact_missing and reports missing / unverified / orphan / retired objects separately (test proves a vanished published artifact is a violation, an unreachable store is 'unverified' with no violation, a retired object is neither). Still not run: real Celery pool kill, broker restart on Redis, transport-level lost ack/redelivery, deployed beat — no Redis server binary exists in this environment and installing one is a global change outside the session's authorization (blocked_external); the memory-transport worker test of T01 remains the only broker evidence. Session 8 (2026-09-10): a disposable Redis became available (Docker Desktop on the host, existing image redis:7.4-alpine, loopback-only container on a dedicated port with a random password and AOF appendfsync always; removed at the end). backend/tests/test_transport_drills.py (5, PostgreSQL + TEST_REDIS_URL, skipped otherwise) starts real prefork workers (concurrency 1) and beat as child processes of the test with the deployed queue/acks_late/reject_on_worker_lost/prefetch/time-limit settings (test deviations: lease 4 s / renew 2 s, visibility_timeout 4 s in the redelivery drills, beat periods 2 s, mock providers with an ASR gate file): a SIGKILLed pool child is requeued at once by the worker, the copy meets the live lease (already_running), the lease lapses by itself, the sweep republishes and the job completes on attempt 2 with one settlement; a SIGKILLed whole worker leaves the delivery parked in Redis unacked, recovery proceeds from the lease alone, and the parked copy restored after the visibility timeout is inert; a visibility-timeout redelivery to a second worker during a live attempt is rejected by the renewed lease; a graceful broker restart keeps a published delivery (AOF) and the worker reconnects, a publication during a broker outage is deferred with last_error and swept later; real beat schedules the dispatch and lease sweeps that publish a never-published intent and recover a vanished worker's job. Every drill ends with empty invariants, one settlement per meeting and an empty queue/unacked set. Product change: broker_transport_options.visibility_timeout is now the hard time limit (JOB_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS + 60) so the broker never redelivers a live attempt (ADR 0008 amendment); the queue-contract test's broker switch now resets Celery's cached result backend and producer pool, which had made the Redis parametrisation time out after the memory one. Not run: the deployed compose stack, a hard kill of the Redis process, the hard time-limit timer itself (its kill path is), PgBouncer, remote CI (the redis marker is skipped when TEST_REDIS_URL is unset; CI sets it, but has not run). Verification with the final code: test_queue_routing (6) + drills 4/5 in one run (9 passed) and drills 1-3 after two test-only fixes (3 passed); whole suite minus the drills 210 passed on PostgreSQL 16.15 as homayar_app; SQLite 5 passed + 5 drills skipped; ruff clean. Product commit 21c32b98.

dependency_note: Validated in local scope only (PostgreSQL 16 as homayar_app, disposable Redis container, mock providers): the deployed compose stack, remote CI, real S3 conditional writes and PgBouncer are unverified; the empty-transcript charging policy (ADR 0003) is an open business decision.
